review_highlights.comment: Extremely good PROFESSOR. There is a decent chunk of work (you can still get an A without putting 100% in tho) but he leaves you kinda wanting to engage in the content. Really enjoyed this class - it is not a 3000 level course in terms of sociology and was able to understand it well without having any background. All of the material covered in class was very applicable to the world and is referred to often by several other professors in other departments.

Frenette is goated. He's knowledgeable about his field and enjoys teaching, making class interesting. Gives lots of feedback on assignments and grades easily. 20-page readings before each class, 3 1-page papers, 1 midterm, 1 interview project, and 1 6-8 pg final paper. Lots of work but the class made me leave my comfort zone and was very rewarding.

Truly a wonderful professor! More work than a typical intro class, but very manageable (~20m reading before each class). Only 1 midterm, but easy to do well if you pay attention. After that, just a few 1-question pop quizzes on readings. Final presentation+paper on an interview instead of an exam. I took it for a premed req, but learned a lot!

Professor Frenette was an incredible educator. His lectures were interesting and engaging. He made sociology exciting and relevant. He always treated students with kindness and understanding, and made himself available outside of class to offer help. His feedback on assignments was detailed and personalized. He is such a joy to learn from.

review_highlights.comment: Is she a terrible professor? Absolutely. I think she has good intentions, but she is not self-aware enough to see how she comes off. analysis.name: Josh Bond
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment:
Very down-to-earth professor with engaging lectures. Easy to reach by email and available after class for questions. Slides are posted and helpful for exams.

Highly recommend going to class since practice problems in class usually appear in some way on exams.

He also uses Counter Strike as an example when teaching OOP so he's goated.

I thought Bond was a great professor, though I found 1101 to be very challenging as it was my first experience with programming. Granted, I skipped the majority of classes so that was likely the main culprit of my lack of success. All the content on the exams are taught to you, and he posts all his lecture slides.

His lectures move very fast, but his slides are detailed and he always posts them after the lecture. There are lots of TAs with office hours throughout the week. Programming assignments were sometimes long, but you pay attention in class/take good notes then they're not too difficult (especially if you have previous coding experience).

Really nice professor. More lenient about homework and other things. Ok lecturer, but new so maybe will get better. Class is also super boring. Random in class questions in class to take attendance. If you could get these questions from someone you probably don't need lecture. Is more comprehensive about what will be on exams.

Not a good lecturer - students would literally correct him during class. Would kinda just read off the slides without really explaining, and I often felt I was just better off skipping class and reading the textbook. Attendance mandatory for 70% of the classes, and the exams were all pretty easy.

analysis.name: Gina Bai
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lots of content, but she makes it easy to understand, and lecture slides are very well done so you can easily go back to reread later or if you miss class. She makes a strong effort to get to know and help students, especially if you participate in class and/or talk to her outside of class. Assignments are challenging but doable and you learn a lot

I loved this class with Dr. Bai! She is very open to questions. She frequently pauses during lecture to make sure the class is understanding the content. This class does have quite a fair amount of PA's (Java), but they were all directly related to the concepts in class. She is one of the sweetest and caring professors you will ever take!

I don't know why people are leaving harsh ratings - I thought Dr. Bai was excellent. I had 0 coding experience before 1101 and found it to be quite easy thanks to her lectures. If you find it tough, do the Zybook before class so that lecture is your second time seeing the material. I had a disagreement about TA feedback on the PA, and she helped.

Took 2201 with professor Bai over prof. Roth because the latter professor had no seats left. I was pleasantly surprised by professor Bai's enthusiasm in teaching and she wanted to make sure every student understood the concepts taught in class by giving good analogies and explaining many times to certain people. Just make sure to attend classes.

Dr. Bai is an incredible professor and if you have the chance to take her, you definitely should. If you aren't interested in CS, the class would be pretty difficult. However, as a CS major, I found the class to be super enjoyable and it has made me excited to continue taking CS courses. Dr. Bai's lectures are the best I've ever seen, by far.

My favorite professors EVER. So caring and compassionate, the most supportive environment I've ever seen fostered in a class. She is quite literally the highlight of my week. Super funny, sweet, and good at conveying the material covered in class. I'm already trying to get her again for next semester.

analysis.name: Brenda Enriquez

A 57 questions syllabus quiz? Are you for real?

I dreaded going to this class each week.

Only good thing is you can drop a lab unit and you work in a group.

Dr. Florian is an incredible professor, however, be prepared to work. Start projects early, go to office hours, and you will succeed.

LOVED DR. FAZIO! Easily my favorite class at Vanderbilt. Every assignment has clear guidelines, tests and quizzes are straightforward, plus she shows lots of cute videos in almost every lecture. Very approachable and clearly wants her students to do well. Also, no final!

This rating is for psy-pc 2300. very sweet prof but she gives SO MUCH reading. every class there was a quiz on abt 60 textbook pages worth of reading hw. class was a little boring/repetitive but other than the hw it was pretty easy

review_highlights.comment: This was the most unique class I have taken. He is a very eccentric person. The class involves a fictional story line about a french monster and grades by giving you "xp". There is never a dull moment in this class and it is very easy to get an A. But he does require external participation. The online textbook is expensive and annoying.

Very fun environment. He is a creative professor who makes his entire course an adventure. Throughout the course you complete three projects, so find a good partner at the begining of the course! He speaks mostly in French at this level which really helped me improve. He is always really helpful if you have a question, and is great to laugh with!

Interesting class set-up. You earn xp by participating in and outside of class which helps progress your grade. It's easy to get an A, as Alexis grades kindly and gives many opportunities to earn xp. As others have said, the online textbook is required for homework and it's very expensive. I had fun in this class.

Taking 1103 with & he's an amazing professor; passionate about linguistics and you can see it in the way he crafts the lessons. I would say the class is more review self pace, so you can def get behind. he is always willing to answer what ever questions you may have. As someone with limited French knowledge, I am glad to have him here.

I absolutely love Alexis. He's an amazing professor and makes every day in the classroom so much fun. He uses an adventure-based curriculum and makes it fun to work towards the grade you want. It's a flipped classroom situation and he gives great feedback and minimal assessments. There's no way to lower your grade, only ways to raise it!

analysis.name: Fatima  Kola

Def take a MHS course with her!

Professor Kola is awesome.  She is by far the best Professor or Teacher I have ever had.  She is knowledgeable, kind, inspirational, supportive, interesting, and very compelling in her delivery.  I would recommend this class to all and I hope that I can take more classes with Professor Kola.  She is so knowledgeable and has enthused me profoundly.

Prof Kola is an outstanding Professor. I would highly recommend this class. The classes were intellectually stimulating and very interesting. I learnt so much and broadened my horizons profoundly. She is extremely brilliant, kind, caring and very respectful of students. Every medical student and Physician should have this knowledge. Excellent class

Dr. Kola is an amazing professor! You have to do a lot of reading but it's a literature class, after all. If you pace yourself it's not too bad. Really appreciated the document she gives out to help us keep track of our own assignments. It made me feel like she really sees us adults. As a prof, she's so smart, caring, interesting, and kind. 10/10.

This is the best class I've ever taken at Vandy! Prof Kola is so smart and the class actually inspires you to want to read and learn. She's an incredible lecturer and person, so caring and kind. I wish I could take every class with her! Enroll in this class, you will NOT regret it.

review_highlights.comment: Attend class. Easily one of my favorite courses in the Spanish department. Professor Falconi made what was an otherwise exceptionally boring required class super enjoyable and added a lot of life. He also cared for his students outside of class as well, which was very appreciated.

Prof Falconi was great, especially facilitating group discussions and getting everyone to feel comfortable speaking spanish in front of each other. He would often go on tangents, but they almost always related to class material and made it more engaging. We only had one paper and a presentation, but participation was needed in this course.

Falconi is genuinely hilarious. More often than not, his lectures turn into personal stories and tangents. He's forgiving in his grading of his writing assignments. His tests can be somewhat challenging, but they're not the end of the world. Take him for his personality. You won't regret it.

I loved Prof. Falconí and his class. Super great guy that is really easy to talk to. My Spanish ability skyrocketed in his class; really easy to understand and has tons of grammar practice exercises. The tests weren't walks in the park, but were very doable if you understand the MindTap concepts and do all of the practice work.

I took him first semester so I saught him out for CORE, that's how much I like him.

Finkelman is an amazing professor! He teaches extremely well and his lectures are very engaging. He is very knowledgeable and loves discussing your questions and interpreations of the course content! He assigns a lot of reading but they are all foundational to the lectures. 10/10 professor and 100% recommend taking a class with him!

Dr. Finkelman is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about Jewish History. His lectures are very informative and give you exactly what you need to know for the debates and essays. There is a lot of reading, but reading it before class is a great way to be prepared for the lecture and participate (which is a big chunk of the grade). Take him!!

Learned so much from this class. It's actually a ton of reading that you need to do so I spent more time on this class than most, but it pays off. Only graded on a take home midterm + final paper, a film response paper, and 3 short quizzes. Super straightforward and prof is not a harsh grader. Only 8 AM i've taken that I was excited to go to.

Really nice genuine guy and not very difficult. Definitely appreciates participation in his classes, but is not super strict about it. He provides really interesting insights for discussions and provides very honest perspectives.

Absolute goat, very understanding and is just an all around specimen. Could save the titanic

Imagine getting paid to be a professor and you're never even there for your lab section. If I had other responsibilities outside of this job I wouldn't be hogging all the lab sections, university should get another professor to run the other sections at that point.

Had him for the 2nd portion of cell bio, the most discouraging, mean, bad-temepered prof I've encountered. analysis.name: Leonora Williamson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Please take Professor Williamson's class. It is, by far, the class I learned the most in and actually enjoyed going to class to. She is incredibly accomplished, well-respected, has a natural talent to make the lectures very engaging, and an impressive network that allowed us to meet so many interesting people. Highly recommend!

Professor Williamson genuinely wants you to learn and cares about the topics. She structures class very well and is veryyyy organized with her material. There are no "surprises" and if you stay on top of work and do what you are supposed to do, you will do very well in this course. Guest speakers are AWESOME and you learn lots from them!

Professor Williamson is one of the few professors at Vandy who genuinely cares about getting to know their students and wants to help them both in and out of the classroom. You have to participate, show up to class, and put effort into your work, but it is beyond worth it. The material, guest speakers, and projects are all relevant and interesting!

Amazing professor, life-long mentor and a gem of Vanderbilt's business department. Prof. Williamson has a very impressive background that actually translates into stories, life lessons, and invaluable advice. Plus, the group project is a great addition to the resume. Just show up, be proactive, and I guarantee that it will be fun and interesting.

I really enjoyed the format of this course. In the lectures, professor Williamson doesn't overestimate how much students know, and she gives students plenty of time to ask questions about concepts. While participation can be stressful for some, professor Williamson offers a multiple different ways to participate, such as anonymous TopHat polls.

analysis.name: Simon Lilburn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: amazing australian dude. open ai and open note everything with attendance quizzes (can drop 4), a midterm, and a final. lots of room for extra credit. easy to not pay attention, but course content has been super applicable to my other classes so highly recommend putting in effort. hes a joy to be around!

Prof. Lilburn is the best teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. He's fun, approachable, and always looking out for his students. There are weekly problem sets where AI is allowed. The take-home midterm and final are fair and also AI allowed, and his random quizzes are easy. I learned a lot and his funny backgrounds make class great. Definitely recommend

I don't have anything more to say than amazing! He's hilarious, very engaging class, so accessible and understanding outside of class. Ton of bright space quizzes but with unlimited attempts - you have to be in class to take them but you should be going to class anyways. It is a lot of content at some points but he is always helpful!

Couldn't say more good things about this professor! Extremely responsive outside the classroom and loves to make Garfield dad jokes during lectures that keep you somewhat engaged. Tons of extra credit meaning you might not even have to take the final. Makes you actually interested in coding and data science.

Incredibly nice professor. Good energy. Not the biggest fan of his lecture style which would involve like 100 slide power points with like a few lines of code on each. Random quizzes for attendance. Easy class overall.

Professor Wisniewski is the most caring professor, and I highly recommend everyone to take his class. I had a wonderful experience learning from him, and his corny jokes will always bring a smile to your face. Highly recommend!! :)

Mark is an amazing professor, and I would have him as a professor many times if I could! It is evident he is passionate about the subject he teaches, and he is very caring to his students. review_highlights.comment: I highly recommend this class, it's fun and you learn a lot. Do not need heavy background in sports and Excel, but you mainly use Excel to complete problems. There are weekly quizzes that are take home and similar to class work. Attendance matters and helps a lot for quizzes. There is a final exam at the end.

Lapre is a great professor and he does a great job of teaching the content in a way that is clear and understandable. Attendance is mandatory and you're not allowed to have tech in most of the classes, but he is very engaging. There are 6 quizzes and a final exam that is all multiple choice. Probably my favorite business mod I have taken so far.

Class was incredibly easy if you just pay attention. Attendance is mandatory, but you receive credit for going. Dr. Lapré is the best, he cares so much about his students. Start a conversation with him, he's a great guy!

Very engaging and really cares about the material and students. Quizzes aren't hard if you do in class work. Class is very organized and is more quantitative (use excel a lot). Topics are really interesting even if you aren't into sports

Great prof, one of the better business modules. Prof breaks down the content clearly with full, printed slides. Do the practice problems before the quizzes, and those will prepare you for the final well. No tech in class, but if you spend the time listening, it makes the quizzes and such easier.

They is one of the nicest people I have ever met! Office hours were always very fun and I felt very comfortable even though I was honestly a little afraid from their brutish appearance at first. Highly recommend!

Cannot say enough good things about Dr. Clinton. By far one of the most caring profs at Vanderbilt and is genuinely interested in seeing students succeed. Class was extremely interesting with multiple exams where the lowest is dropped.

Professor Clinton is quirky as hell (basically I just mean nerdy) but like in a good way. He's so fun to listen to when he lectures about polling because you can just tell he's so (overly) passionate about the subject. He does talk really (and I mean really) fast but just learn to accept that about him. Highly enjoyable nevertheless!

Professor Clinton is such a nice guy and so understanding as a professor. Took him for intro to quant. poli sci--the quizzes you can retake as many times and exams are all very doable. Super into content and just a great, nice guy. Really recommend him
Great class and truly an amazing professor. His class is actually worth the tuition. Not difficult to get an A as long as you put some effort into the problem sets and ask questions

analysis.name: Clint Hendrix
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hendrix is an amazing professor and an even better person. In core, he made sure that all students understood the material. Also, he seeked feedback from students a lot about the course. He is a really nice guy, super funny, and cares a lot about his students. Whether it's for a language class or core, take Dr. Hendrix.

Clint has been the best professor I have met at Vandy. He is funny, welcoming and understanding. He makes an effort to meet you where you are at if you are struggling. The class is heavy in grammar, but Clint helps you make the jump from an intermediate to advanced Spanish speaker. I am taking him again this semester, and nothing but good things!!

Prof. Hendrix is the perfect professor for someone with beginner or intermediate Spanish skills. He's kind, professional, and funny and doesn't make class difficult either — if you show up and do the necessary work, you shouldn't have a problem getting a good grade. He makes up for a relatively dull class with his personality.

Hendrix is by far my favorite Spanish prof in the department. He's verrry funny and helps with those tricky aspects of the language that are more difficult for American students. He's also a really fair grader. He made me want to continue with the language past the intermediate level. Wish I could have fit it into my schedule.

Man, I love Clint. Had him for 2203 and spent a lot of time watching funny cat videos and talking about current events. He gives great feedback and even though the class is 4 days a week (you get Wednesdays off), he's a riot and makes the commitment totally worth it. Put in the effort and you'll see the results

Hard class is just bc lot of content.

dr. clements is a nice person, but his teaching style didn't resonate with me. he moved fast to cover a ton of content, so you have to do a lot of independent study, but even then you can get very lost. i put a ton of effort into his section and still didn't do well, and not even patton's section could bring me back up. harder than gen chem imo.

Dr. Clements is very caring and approachable. Content is covered for about 20 minutes in class(flipped) and the worksheet is completed the rest of class. I found this style to be difficult since the content was sped through and required previous understanding. The test questions were extremely out of the box and were advanced for an intro class.

His content is hard, but Clements has lots of office hours. He provides a lot of content due to the flipped classroom, so be prepared to do a lot of work outside class. It is annoying that he covers a lot of topics in greater depth than we need to know them, but he doesn't test a lot on things he doesn't teach. Tests weren't awful but not easy.

Nice enough guy. The exams are really brutal in a non-constructive way. Preaches "application" of content but tends to get insanely in the weeds and far-fetched with exam questions, such as his little stint over CRISPR. Did well in the class but had to literally live and breathe the content, which shouldn't be the case for a 1000-level class.

Clayton brings a unique love for the arts to policy discussion. Extremely well-versed in media across the board, the class hinges on participation and reading/watching the course content. Ultimately a pretty cool class with low work load and caring professor. Take for sure w/ an interest specifically in sci-fi or the intersection of art + policy

Cizmar is such a caring professor and makes class super fun to be in. She really knows what she's talking about and can easily jump in at any moment and help you exactly where you're at. She also is incredibly human and relatable.

Good professor but sometimes hard to understand. Lecture notes are clear and I learn a lot from them. Super Great guy. I thought he was a phenomenal professor who prepared us aptly for the exams. Everything I missed throughout the course was my own fault. Phenomenal for Linear, and I assume everything else too.

I had heard from friends that Professor Somer-Topcu is an extremely hard grader and signed up for 210 reluctantly. After taking a couple tests now though, I can confidently say that her test formats are extremely easy (longest portion is 1-page essays). She also tries to make class interesting through relevant videos, Daily Show clips, etc.

Her difficulty is vastly overrated here.  Her debate grades are very high and her tests averages were somewhere in the 80s.  Her class is not that hard, as she gives you a study guide with topics to know.  It is memorization, but that's what most PSCI classes are.  She expects people to read and walked out on her class when they did not.
